answer_summary: runtime.dll entry function at RVA 0x139238F opens with a heavy MSVC-style prologue (8 GPR pushes: rbp, r15, r14, r13, r12, rsi, rdi, rbx; sub rsp, 0x778 = 1.9 KB stack; lea rbp, [rsp+0x80] frame; 10 XMM saves xmm15..xmm6 to [rbp+0x6e0..+0x650]; and rsp,~0x3F for 64-byte align), then jumps FORWARD past ~122 bytes of opaque/junk bytes (jmp 0x1392482) to the real body. The real body begins with `mov rbx, rsp; mov [rbx+0x6c8], rbp` (stashing rbp) then jumps again to skip more junk (jmp 0x13924d5), where the FIRST REAL CALL sits: `call 0x130A4A0` at 0x13924d5, IMMEDIATELY followed by `jmp rax` — the canonical MBA-obfuscated indirect-dispatch stub pattern (helper computes target address into rax, tail-jump transfers). No memory access with a displacement in the 0xC8..0x138 range appears in the prologue or the first real basic block — the frame is addressed at +0x6c8/+0x650..+0x6e0. No FF-15 / FF-90 style indirect calls appear in the first 1024 bytes; indirect dispatch is instead done via `call rel32; jmp rax` MBA pattern. Capstone linear-decoded only 29 real instructions cleanly (through 0x139241E) before hitting the opaque skipped block; resuming at each jump target recovered 250+ more decodes but many mid-block bytes are unreachable data.

RESULT: Rule-2 (FK-31 in-process) = 403 (92.2%); Rule-3 (different-bug-class, all READ faults, 30/32 at RIP low16=0x205D = S111 catalog_store_fix heap scan) = 32; Rule-4 (SUSPECT companion-mediated) = 0; parse errors = 2 (same corrupt .dmp file in two archived dirs). Every one of the 403 Rule-2 dumps carries the exact S131 signature — 0xC0000005 access violation + ExceptionInformation[0]==8 EXECUTE + RIP≡1 (mod 0x1000) + RIP inside a MEM_IMAGE READONLY region whose AllocationBase == (RIP-1)&~0xFFF (the deliberate jump into the manually-mapped runtime.dll DOS header MZ page). The 403 group cleanly across 5 boot-era runtime.dll bases (0x7FFA42600000×11, 0x7FFB57400000×31, 0x7FFCA1400000×15, 0x7FFD3B400000×343, 0x7FFE9B600000×3) — perfectly matching every entry in CLAUDE.md's per-boot FK-31 kill-address register, and adding independent confirmation for the two most recent eras (S157). ZERO Rule-4 hits ⇒ no evidence of JIT-stub or thread-stack RIPs; the FK-31 kill vector never lands in MEM_PRIVATE RWX. Crashwatch corpus scan of 19 `docs/crashwatch*.log` files found 4 confirmed Rule-1 FK-32 events (exit 0x0000DEAD, no minidump: s145×2, s146×1, s147 flight5×1) plus 5 operator TerminateProcess(-1) cleanups and 1 clean exit. VERDICT: The corpus decisively supports FK-31 as in-process (the companion may spawn 0xDEAD FK-32 kills, but the 0xC0000005 FK-31 death class is a self-fault in the game process's own manually-mapped runtime.dll page). This is a REFUTATION of the "companion mediates FK-31" hypothesis at n=403.

notes: Tool details: existing scratchpad/classify_fk_dumps.py (pre-existing from earlier session work — I ran, aggregated, and audited it, did not author from scratch) uses direct MDMP stream parsing rather than shelling out to mdctx.py per-file (much faster for a 437-file batch). Rules 1–4 implemented as documented in the task. Parses ExceptionStream (6), ThreadList (3), ModuleList (4), MemoryInfoListStream (16). MemoryInfoListStream is what enables Rule-2/Rule-4 discrimination — it carries per-region State/Protect/Type/AllocationBase for every VA range, so a RIP in a MEM_IMAGE READONLY region (Rule 2 baseline) vs MEM_PRIVATE RWX (Rule 4 SUSPECT) is a direct read, not an inference. 2 files failed with 'not MDMP' (same GUID appears in two archived crashpad dirs, likely a truncated/quarantined dup). No other errors. Per-file JSON at C:\\Users\\eastr\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\claude\\...\\scratchpad\\classifications_final.json (435 entries) for auditability. Classifier can be re-run in ~2s per pass. Note: task says Rule 3 is 'other RIPs (not runtime.dll+1)' and Rule 4 is 'MEM_PRIVATE RWX or thread stack' — my classifier correctly separates these: Rule-3 in output means 'other fault class where RIP is neither on stack nor in MEM_PRIVATE RWX', preserving the semantic distinction (all 32 Rule-3 dumps are ordinary in-process READ faults with RIP on shim heap). Not obtained: exit-code data for the minidump-generating deaths (crashwatch.out.log gets truncated per-launch, so historical exit codes for the 435 classified minidumps aren't recoverable) — but the minidump ExceptionCode 0xC0000005 is a direct instrument for that class and the FK-31 attribution rests on it plus the region signature, not on exit code.
